reason: E2 shows refractory elements strengthen Ti and Ni alloys via solid solution strengthening, supporting the first premise, but it does not address HEAs with Ti and Ni as primary constituents, nor does it support precipitation hardening or improved ductility. E1 and E3 concern different alloy systems (TiVNbTa and HfMoNbTaW) without Ti and Ni, and E1 actually shows softening from impurities, contradicting the claimed mechanism. The key premises about the specific HEA system, precipitation hardening, and ductility improvement lack direct evidence.
premises: Refractory elements (Mo, W, Re) provide strong solid solution strengthening in Ti and Ni alloys
Refractory elements improve elevated-temperature strength in advanced alloys
Solid solution strengthening and precipitation hardening are the operative mechanisms
The intervention will improve both strength and ductility
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase Ti-Ni-containing HEAs above 700°C
